title: Measure Less, Know More: Self-Supervised Test-Time Feature Acquisition
claim: A learned policy sequentially acquires a few input features, moving through latent space to approximate the full-input representation without knowing the downstream task.
layout: Single panel, iterations flow bottom-right to top over latent-space blob, ECHO-k badge left
description: A single panel shows a light gray-blue blob labeled 'latent space of model'. A trajectory of circles, shaded from pale to dark blue, curves through the blob. It starts at 'iteration 1' at lower right, goes through 'iteration 2' on the right, then dots for omitted steps, then 'iteration k' at lower center. It ends at a double-ringed dark-blue node at the top. Each circle is tied to a small 3x2 grid of pink and red squares. The grid fills in as iterations proceed: iteration 1 has one filled cell, and the top node's grid, labeled 'all modalities and features', is fully filled. A dotted arrow runs from the top node to 'downstream tasks'. A rounded 'ECHO-k' box at left holds the same four-shade circle sequence as a legend. The eye goes first to the large ECHO-k label, then follows the arrows.
caption: \ours learns an RL policy to iteratively selects views to approximate the full latent representation learned by any pretrained model, without any knowledge of downstream tasks. Once learned, the policy can be deployed for budgeted feature acquisition.
abstract: Recent progress in multimodal, high-dimensional learning has enabled foundation models to process heterogeneous, large-scale data. However, at test time, acquiring all features or modalities can be prohibitively costly and often redundant. Sequentially selecting informative modalities is therefore critical, yet challenging when the downstream task or prediction target is unknown. To this end, we introduce ECHO-$k$, a task-agnostic and self-supervised learning principle for modality acquisition: we use a deep model's internal pretrained representations (e.g., from a foundation model) as proxy targets that summarize cross-modal information. We provide theoretical guarantees in a stylized linear setting that motivate a reinforcement learning (RL) policy for sequential modality selection. Across task-agnostic and label-free acquisition baselines, ECHO-$k$ consistently improves budgeted downstream performance across diverse foundation-model backends. Our method provides a principled route to cost-aware test-time deployment, with implications for any multimodal system where measurements are expensive or time-constrained, and downstream tasks unknown a priori.
